title: Cross-client denial queue and appeal drafts for outsourced medical billing companies (Tebra first)

fixture.label: queue #11 benchmark case R2: a real opportunity from queue #10 (the billing-company runner-up); the appetite is a test fixture

upstream_status.summary: Runner-up since 2026-10-02 (its opportunity brief: 'still close to a kill'). Queue #10 (2026-10-03): not validated; no original deal-breaker failed; two open fatal unknowns (exact rival; $20 against labour); ranked second. The owner's decision is pending.

buyer: Small and mid-size outsourced medical billing companies that work claims for independent physician groups on practice-management (PM) systems without post-denial AI appeal drafting, Tebra first
user: The billing company's billers and appeals lead, who work denials across all the firm's clients
job: Turn the 835 remittances the firm already posts, across all its clients, into one denial queue sorted by denial reason (CARC/RARC), filing deadline and dollars, and draft payer-specific appeal letters that the firm's staff review and send.

evidence.claim: NDS InfoServ's AI appeals page names RCM companies that manage appeals across multiple clients among its buyers.
evidence.quote: RCM companies managing appeals at scale across multiple clients

evidence.claim: Muni Health's blog names small-to-mid-size billing companies that handle their own appeals among those its $20-per-appeal product is right for.
evidence.quote: Who it's right for: Independent practices, small-to-mid-size billing companies, and specialty groups that handle their own appeals.

evidence.claim: EZAppeal's buyer's guide says it is built for billing companies.
evidence.quote: EZAppeal is built specifically for billing companies.

evidence.claim: EZAppeal's pricing page names billing companies as buyers, signs a BAA with every account, triage free, $5 per drafted letter.
evidence.quote: For billing companies, practices and utilization review teams. Every account signs a Business Associate Agreement. Triage is free; drafted letters are $5 each, less on a plan.

evidence.claim: EZAppeal lists as its own limitation one login per account with no team workspaces; no cross-client queue is stated.
evidence.quote: One login per account: no team workspaces or role-based access

evidence.claim: EZAppeal drafts the appeal from the payer's policy when one is on file.
evidence.quote: When a denial needs a letter, EZAppeal drafts the appeal or prior authorization request from the payer's policy when one is on file

evidence.claim: NDS drafts a payer-specific appeal letter.
evidence.quote: drafts a complete appeal letter tailored to the denial type and payer.

evidence.claim: NDS routes classified denials into work queues by denial type, payer and dollar amount; the page does not say one queue spans several client practices. Sold by demo, no published price.
evidence.quote: Routes classified denials into intelligent work queues based on configurable rules - by denial type, payer, dollar amount, complexity, or any combination your organization defines.

evidence.claim: Medi, a billing-company RCM platform (waitlist only), states one queue across every client; no appeal drafting is stated.
evidence.quote: One queue across every client. Your appeals lead sees the denials.

evidence.claim: Medi replaces Tebra (a cutover onto Medi) rather than working on Tebra clients' data.
evidence.quote: The pattern that protects revenue is a forward-only cutover on Medi with legacy A/R closeout running in parallel inside Tebra.

evidence.claim: Tebra sells billing companies a multi-client dashboard inside its billing software.
evidence.quote: Manage all clients in one dashboard, regardless of EHR

evidence.claim: Tebra Billing includes denial tracking.
evidence.quote: Track denials, reimbursements, and collections in real time

evidence.claim: Tebra's September 2026 release added Similar Denied Claims to its pre-submission AI Claim Review; no appeal drafting is described.
evidence.quote: The AI Claim Review feature included in Tebra's AI Billing Assistant now has Similar Denied Claims

evidence.claim: Tebra's API terms (section 4.4) bar using the Tebra API to replicate or compete with Tebra's core products, which leaves the manual 835 export.
evidence.quote: You may not use the Tebra API to replicate or compete with core products or services offered by Tebra

evidence.claim: Muni Health: 3 free appeals, then $20 per appeal (drafting only).
evidence.quote: Start with 3 free appeals. Then $20 per appeal.

evidence.claim: US median hourly wage (BLS 2025, via O*NET) for billing and posting clerks (SOC 43-3021) is $23.32, unloaded.
evidence.quote: Median wages (2025) $23.32 hourly, $48,500 annual

evidence.claim: SOC 43-3021 covers the billers who work denials (job titles include Biller and Billing Specialist).
evidence.quote: Sample of reported job titles: Biller, Billing Accounts Representative, Billing Clerk, Billing Coordinator, Billing Specialist

evidence.claim: A TextExpander marketing blog says manual appeal letters take 50-70 minutes each, with no sample or source (unmeasured).
evidence.quote: Your billing team spends 50-70 minutes drafting each appeal letter

evidence.claim: The same vendor blog puts unloaded labour at $18-26 per appeal ($22 an hour).
evidence.quote: At an average billing specialist salary of $22 per hour, that's $18-26 in labor cost per appeal

evidence.claim: Billing companies typically charge 4-10% of collections; in Tebra's 2022 survey 24.5% of those on this model charged 6-7%.
evidence.quote: Many teams quote a typical range of 4-10%. In Tebra's survey , 24.5% of billing companies that used this model charged 6-7% in 2022

evidence.claim: Health Affairs Scholar 2026 (2019 Inovalon multipayer data, professional claims): 60.8% of initially denied MA claims were ultimately paid (never-appealed denials counted as unpaid; dollar-weighted).
evidence.quote: Medicare Advantage had the highest overturn rate at 60.8% vs 51.1% for Medicaid and 46.4% for commercial

evidence.claim: In that study, final (unrecovered) denials include never-appealed claims as well as claims denied on appeal.
evidence.quote: Final denials include both never-appealed and denied-on-appeal claims

evidence.claim: ASHEcon newsletter: over two-thirds of denied claims are never resubmitted (citing Reiner 2018).
evidence.quote: over two-thirds of denied claims are never resubmitted (Reiner 2018)

evidence.claim: Dunn et al. (remittance data on physician visits): with rework costs and revenue never collected, physicians lose 18% of Medicaid, 4.7% of Medicare and 2.4% of commercial revenue to billing problems.
evidence.quote: Combining these costs with the revenue never collected, we estimate that physicians lose 18% of Medicaid revenue to billing problems, compared with 4.7% for Medicare and 2.4% for commercial insurers

open_unknowns.question: Does a product already sell exactly this to billing companies (one queue across clients built on posted 835s, drafted letters, self-serve or a published price)? Nearest: NDS InfoServ (multi-client RCM buyers, reads 835s, work queues, drafted letters; one queue spanning clients not stated; demo only, no price). Census incomplete: eClinicalWorks, Office Ally, Claim.MD and Availity not read; Infinx, Experian and ClaimCure unreachable.
open_unknowns.source: queue #10 desk_check 648de4ff A1 (unknown, fatal); REPORT.md K6

open_unknowns.question: Does a flat price at or above about $20 per appeal cost billing companies more than the labour it replaces? Minutes per appeal are unmeasured (only a vendor blog's 50-70 minutes); the median biller wage is $23.32 an hour unloaded.
Does each client practice's BAA allow subcontracting to the tool's maker (client by client)?
Do state billing or third-party-administrator rules apply (New Jersey raised)?
What do the code-list licences (CPT, X12) require for a product that reads and shows these codes?
Are the denials billing companies give up on today worth appealing? The 60.8% MA overturn rate is dollar-weighted across all professional claims, and abandoned denials are probably the weaker ones.
Are drafted letters accurate (no made-up facts) and accepted by billers as ready to send? The planned shadow test (queue #10 K3) is not run and needs patient data.

appetite.note: Test fixture for the queue #11 benchmark: not the owner's appetite and not a market-screening time limit.

constraints.text: No patient data in this work (835 remittances carry patient data). Any test with real remittances needs a BAA chain and the owner's go-ahead.
No contact with billing companies, practices, payers or anyone else without the owner's go-ahead; honest tests only (disclosed AI, opt-in contact).
No real money (ads, deposits, paid tools) without the owner's rails and go-ahead.
Tebra API terms 4.4 bar using the Tebra API to replicate or compete with Tebra's core products: only the manual 835 export is usable.
Before the first paid use: HIPAA subcontractor rules (45 CFR 164.502(e)(1)(ii)), with each client practice's BAA allowing subcontracting.

proposed_solution.summary: One queue across all of a billing company's clients sorts the 835 remittances the firm already posts by denial reason (CARC/RARC), filing deadline and dollars, and drafts payer-specific appeal letters; the firm's staff review and send them.

features.name: Cross-client denial queue
features.does: Sort the posted 835 remittances of all clients by denial reason (CARC/RARC), filing deadline and dollars

features.name: Payer-specific appeal drafts
features.does: Draft payer-specific appeal letters for the firm's staff to review and send

notes: Price idea (the hypothesis's, not an owner decision): flat per appeal or per seat per month, not a share of recovered dollars, because a billing company paid 4-10% of collections can't share a percentage of the same dollar. Channel idea (hypothesis): HBMA, search ads on billing-company denial terms, PM partner programmes. Planned but not run (queue #10 K3): a 4-week shadow test at one billing company, at least 300 denied lines across 3 or more clients, 30 drafted letters checked by two billers, and a zero-made-up-facts test; it needs patient data, so it needs the owner's go-ahead.
